presentationBoundary: Content, order, branching, and persistence state are agent data. Spotlight placement, visual anchoring, and animation are client-owned.

skip.label: Skip tour
skip.effect: marks the tour complete; it can be reopened from Preferences

steps.title: Welcome to MSC
steps.body: Let's get your first Minecraft server online. This tour takes about two minutes — we'll do everything together.

steps.title: Your Server List
steps.body: Open your server list to add your first server.

steps.title: Create a Server
steps.body: Choose Add Server to open the server builder.

steps.title: Choose Your Path
steps.body: Start Fresh sets up a brand new server from scratch. It is selected for you.

steps.title: Pick a Type
steps.body: Java is for PC players. Bedrock is for mobile, console, and Windows players.

steps.title: Name Your Server
steps.body: This is a controller label; the world name is set later and can be different.

steps.title: Standard or Modded?
steps.body: Standard servers run plugins; modded servers require every player to install the same mods.

steps.title: Choose Your Software
steps.body: Paper is recommended for standard servers; Fabric is recommended for modded servers.

steps.title: Pick a Version
steps.body: The latest version is selected for most servers; choose a pinned version only when you need one.

steps.title: Bedrock Cross-play
steps.body: Enable this to let Bedrock players join a Java server through Geyser and Floodgate.

steps.title: Xbox Broadcast
steps.body: Enable this to publish the server in the Xbox or console Friends tab.

steps.title: Review Your Settings
steps.body: Review the server choices, then continue to connectivity.

steps.title: How Will Friends Connect?
steps.body: Port forwarding uses your router. A Playit tunnel works without router access and adds relay latency.

steps.title: Set Your Ports
steps.body: The default Java and Bedrock ports work for most setups; change them only when running multiple servers.

steps.title: Ready to Continue
steps.body: Connectivity is configured. Continue to set up the world.

steps.title: Create Your First World
steps.body: Choose a new world, then set its name, difficulty, game mode, and optional seed.

steps.title: Add Plugins or Mods
steps.body: Browse Modrinth or import files now, or add them after creation.

steps.title: Create It
steps.body: Check the summary, give the server a display name, then create it.

steps.title: Back to Home
steps.body: The server is ready. Return to the main screen.

steps.title: Accept the EULA
steps.body: Minecraft requires EULA acceptance before a server can start.

steps.title: Start Your Server
steps.body: Start the server for the first time.

steps.title: Watch It Boot
steps.body: When the log says Done, the server is ready for players.

steps.title: Continue into Details?
steps.body: The server is up. Continue for a quick tour of the Details workspace, or finish the tour.

steps.title: Make More Room
steps.body: Move the divider to give the Details workspace room.

steps.title: Overview
steps.body: Overview is the live home base for status, connections, and server health.

steps.title: Players
steps.body: Players shows the online roster and player tools.

steps.title: Worlds
steps.body: Worlds manages slots, imports, and backups.

steps.title: Packs
steps.body: Packs manages resource packs for this server.

steps.title: Performance
steps.body: Performance shows TPS, memory, CPU, and server health.

steps.title: Components
steps.body: Components manages server software, add-ons, and helpers.

steps.title: Settings
steps.body: Settings changes core server options; changes are saved explicitly.

steps.title: Files
steps.body: Files browses server configs, logs, and world data.

steps.title: You're All Set
steps.body: The server is running. The port-forwarding guide can help friends outside the network join, and the tour can be restarted from Preferences.
